title: Embedding Two-View Knowledge Graphs with Class Inheritance and Structural Similarity

problem.claim: Two-view KG embedding seeks joint vector representations of entities and relations across ontology and instance views.

gap.claim: Existing methods neglect class inheritance hierarchies and structural similarity between the two views.

contributions.claim: CISS is a two-view KG embedding model that incorporates class inheritance and structural similarity.
CISS uses sibling-class sets to learn fine-grained class representations.
CISS constructs a virtual instance-view KG from clustered instances and compares subgraph representations across views.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CISS as a novel two-view KG embedding model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CISS achieves superior performance compared with existing models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Two-view KGs contain ontology classes and instances of those classes, motivating joint embedding of entities and relations.
Class hierarchies create inheritance structure, while existing methods omit class inheritance and cross-view structural similarity.
CISS addresses both omissions using sibling-class sets and virtual instance-view subgraph comparison.
The authors report superior performance against existing models.

source_observation.claim: Instances inherit properties from their corresponding classes, creating structural similarity between ontology-view and instance-view networks.

interpretation.claim: Embedding methods may benefit from explicitly modeling structure shared across related representational views.

application.claim: Construct a view aligned with the original structure and compare corresponding subgraph representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond two-view KGs.

unknowns: Datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and quantitative results are not specified.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for class clustering, virtual KG construction, or representation comparison.
The abstract does not report computational costs or limitations.
